title: Bank agent: service health
description: Live service latency, errors, model behaviour, dependencies, and the VM, from privacy-safe OpenTelemetry metrics (docs/operations/grafana-dashboard.md). No customer data and no offline evaluation results.

panels.title: Requests per second
panels.description: HTTP requests the API answered per second, health probes excluded, for the selected routes. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: 5xx share, last 5 minutes
panels.description: Share of API responses with a 5xx status over the last 5 minutes (all routes). Yellow from 1 percent, red from 5 percent, the ErrorRateSpike alert threshold. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: p95 latency, last 5 minutes
panels.description: 95th percentile of API response time over the last 5 minutes, for the selected routes. Includes model-bound turns. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: p99 latency, last 5 minutes
panels.description: 99th percentile of API response time over the last 5 minutes, for the selected routes. Buckets reach 60 s, so a slow model call is measured, not clamped. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests the API workers are processing right now, summed over workers. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Degradation level
panels.description: Highest degradation level reported by any API worker: L0 normal, L1 fallback model, L2 template-only phrasing, L3 baseline models, L4 database unavailable (docs/operations/degradation.md). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Latency p50, p95, p99 by route
panels.description: API response time percentiles per route template (path parameters are never labels). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Requests per second by status code
panels.description: Request rate split by HTTP status code, for the selected routes. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: 5xx share by route
panels.description: Share of responses with a 5xx status per route. Empty means no server error in the window. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: 4xx by route and status
panels.description: Client errors per second by route and status code: session and step-up checks, validation, customer isolation (another customer's resource answers 404), and rate limits all answer 4xx. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Rate-limit refusals
panels.description: Requests refused by the API's per-IP and per-session rate limits, by limit class and key kind (the key itself is never a label). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Engine turn latency p50, p95, p99 by workflow
panels.description: Time the workflow engine spends on a turn (routing, policy, tools, model calls), per workflow. It excludes the opening database reads and the closing write; compare with the end-to-end panel. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: End-to-end turn request p50, p95, p99
panels.description: Response time of POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/turns as the API measures it: the engine time plus session checks, database reads and writes, and serialization. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Turns per minute by workflow and outcome
panels.description: Stored turns per minute, by workflow and outcome (resolved, clarified, abstained, escalated, refused, in_progress). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Escalated share by workflow
panels.description: Share of turns in the selected period that ended in a handoff to a human, per workflow. The router row counts turns before a workflow is chosen. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Handoffs by reason
panels.description: Handoffs created in the selected period, by reason code (domain/escalation.py). Each handoff carries a structured summary, never a raw transcript. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Model calls per minute by result
panels.description: Logical model calls per minute (retries and failover included in one call): ok, or the error code that ended it. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Model error share, last 15 minutes
panels.description: Share of model calls that ended in an error over the last 15 minutes. A failed call falls back to deterministic templates; it never reaches the customer as an error. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Successful call latency p50, p95, p99 by serving model
panels.description: Duration of model calls that succeeded, by the model that answered (the fallback model appears after a failover). Failures are excluded so an open circuit does not pull the percentiles down. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Tokens per minute against the quota
panels.description: Input plus output tokens per minute by serving model. The red line is the 60,000 tokens-per-minute quota of the production gpt-4.1-mini deployment (gpt-4o has 50,000). Azure counts the requested maximum output against the quota, so throttling can start below the line. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Model calls per minute by serving model
panels.description: Successful model calls per minute by the model that answered. Calls served by the fallback model mean the primary failed (degradation level L1). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Model cost per turn
panels.description: Model cost in the selected period divided by stored turns. Prices come from services/api/config/llm_prices.yaml; an unverified price, or a model without a row, is costed high on purpose (see the price basis panel). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Model cost per resolved turn
panels.description: Model cost in the selected period divided by the turns resolved without a human (the operating efficiency figure of the brief). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Model calls per turn
panels.description: Model calls in the selected period divided by stored turns. Deterministic paths make none. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Cost per hour by serving model and price basis
panels.description: Model spend rate. Price basis verified means a checked list price; unverified and unknown_model are costed at a deliberately higher rate (a safety multiplier, and for a model without a row the highest known price), so the budget errs on the safe side. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Deterministic fallbacks by prompt and reason
panels.description: Model calls replaced by the deterministic path (templates or baselines), by prompt and error code. This is the reliability ladder working, not a customer-facing error. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Circuit state per model
panels.description: Circuit breaker state for each configured model: closed (calls flow), half-open (one trial call), open (calls skipped until the cool-down ends). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Daily model budget used
panels.description: Share of the daily model budget (LLM_DAILY_BUDGET_USD) spent today, the highest value any worker reports. At 1 the gateway refuses model calls and the deterministic path answers. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Degradation level over time
panels.description: Highest degradation level over time. Each step down the ladder keeps the service safe with less model help (docs/operations/degradation.md). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Component state
panels.description: State of each dependency the degradation monitor watches: the primary and fallback model, the model budget, the learned models, the credit catalog, and the database. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Database connections in use
panels.description: Connections checked out of the SQLAlchemy pool. Each API worker has 5 pooled plus 5 overflow connections: the red line is one worker's ceiling. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Database connection failures
panels.description: Failed attempts to reach PostgreSQL. Any value here moves the service to L4 and the DatabaseUnavailable alert fires. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Share of the VM's CPU time not idle, all cores, read by the collector from /proc (not namespaced in the container). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Share of the VM's memory in use (excluding page cache and buffers). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Run-queue length averaged over 1, 5, and 15 minutes; compare with the VM's 2 vCPUs. Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.

panels.title: Root disk used
panels.description: Share of the OS disk in use (images, volumes, logs, and backups live there). Live telemetry from the running service, not offline evaluation.
